k: Round two! Brothers in arms, brothers in debt — KELL THE NET and KELL THE FIST!
src: 'Round two! Brothers in arms, brothers in debt — KELL THE NET and KELL THE FIST!'

k: The final round! He has eaten three gates and a herald — GRIZZLEMAW!
src: 'The final round! He has eaten three gates and a herald — GRIZZLEMAW!'

k: Round one! Imported at great expense from the Sunscar — the GLASS SCORPIONS! Do not step on them. They hate that.
src: 'Round one! Imported at great expense from the Sunscar — the GLASS SCORPIONS! Do not step on them. They hate that.'

k: Round two! Fastest blade in the Heartland, slowest to pay his tab — SERENO THE SWIFT!
src: 'Round two! Fastest blade in the Heartland, slowest to pay his tab — SERENO THE SWIFT!'

k: The final round! Forged in the bell foundries from a broken bell and a bad idea — THE IRON BULL!
src: 'The final round! Forged in the bell foundries from a broken bell and a bad idea — THE IRON BULL!'

k: Round one! Dredged from the Fens at tremendous personal risk — the MIRE LURKERS!
src: 'Round one! Dredged from the Fens at tremendous personal risk — the MIRE LURKERS!'

k: Round two! One prays, one curses, neither has ever lost — the MASKS OF DAWN AND DUSK!
src: 'Round two! One prays, one curses, neither has ever lost — the MASKS OF DAWN AND DUSK!'

k: The final round! Mother of a thousand, mercy for none — THE SCYTHE MATRON!
src: 'The final round! Mother of a thousand, mercy for none — THE SCYTHE MATRON!'

k: Round one! They ride the bells' own echoes — the STORM KITES!
src: 'Round one! They ride the bells\' own echoes — the STORM KITES!'

k: Round two! Three shields, one wall, no gaps — the PHALANX OF AURENNE!
src: 'Round two! Three shields, one wall, no gaps — the PHALANX OF AURENNE!'

k: The championship! Forty-one bouts. Forty-one wins. Your champion, and mine — VALKA THE UNDEFEATED!
src: 'The championship! Forty-one bouts. Forty-one wins. Your champion, and mine — VALKA THE UNDEFEATED!'

k: Not bad! Here — a few tonics for your trouble.
src: 'Not bad! Here — a few tonics for your trouble.'

k: Six kinds! Take my lucky coin. It never once brought me luck, but it might like you better.
src: 'Six kinds! Take my lucky coin. It never once brought me luck, but it might like you better.'

k: Nine! You've got the hands for it. These fruits came all the way from the Sunscar.
src: 'Nine! You\'ve got the hands for it. These fruits came all the way from the Sunscar.'

k: Twelve species. My old guild brooch — the Crests in it still turn.
src: 'Twelve species. My old guild brooch — the Crests in it still turn.'

k: Every fish in the world. Every one. I... take this. You've earned something that matters.
src: 'Every fish in the world. Every one. I... take this. You\'ve earned something that matters.'

k: A Halloway without a rod? Shameful. Take my spare.
src: 'A Halloway without a rod? Shameful. Take my spare.'

k: Greer Thackery, the Collegium's bestiarist, has posted five marks: rare beasts of the old roads. Hunt them, then tell her by the canal bridge in Aurenne. She also pays for new kinds of creature in the Compendium.
src: 'Greer Thackery, the Collegium\'s bestiarist, has posted five marks: rare beasts of the old roads. Hunt them, then tell her by the canal bridge in Aurenne. She also pays for new kinds of creature in the Compendium.'

k: Greer Thackery survived the Sundering and keeps the Ledger in Keelhaven now. Five new marks are posted, and any old mark still alive came through the Sundering too. Hunt them all, then tell her.
src: 'Greer Thackery survived the Sundering and keeps the Ledger in Keelhaven now. Five new marks are posted, and any old mark still alive came through the Sundering too. Hunt them all, then tell her.'

k: Strike a weakness and the book remembers it. Watch a beast's moves and they go in too. Fell a few of a kind and you'll learn how it thinks.
src: 'Strike a weakness and the book remembers it. Watch a beast\'s moves and they go in too. Fell a few of a kind and you\'ll learn how it thinks.'

k: You've the look of Lanternfall, girl. Salt in the eyes.
src: 'You\'ve the look of Lanternfall, girl. Salt in the eyes.'

k: My gran was a Tidecaller. You'll not have heard of it. The Choir struck it from the rolls when the fishing towns stopped paying tithe — said the sea was a heathen thing to sing to.
src: 'My gran was a Tidecaller. You\'ll not have heard of it. The Choir struck it from the rolls when the fishing towns stopped paying tithe — said the sea was a heathen thing to sing to.'

k: Struck it out of the books, but they couldn't strike it out of the water. Gran said the last Tidecaller's crest-glass went down with the last singer, out past the strait. She's still out there, singing. I hear her some nights.
src: 'Struck it out of the books, but they couldn\'t strike it out of the water. Gran said the last Tidecaller\'s crest-glass went down with the last singer, out past the strait. She\'s still out there, singing. I hear her some nights.'

k: If the sea's gone, maybe the song is all that's left of it. Go and listen. Take it back, if she'll let you.
src: 'If the sea\'s gone, maybe the song is all that\'s left of it. Go and listen. Take it back, if she\'ll let you.'

k: Grandmother Wend in Keelhaven says the last Tidecaller's crest-glass lies at the far east end of the Strait That Was, still guarded by its singer.
src: 'Grandmother Wend in Keelhaven says the last Tidecaller\'s crest-glass lies at the far east end of the Strait That Was, still guarded by its singer.'

k: Past the last bridge, at the very end of the strait. Listen for her.
src: 'Past the last bridge, at the very end of the strait. Listen for her.'

k: You found her. I heard it last night — the singing stopped. Thank you for letting her rest.
src: 'You found her. I heard it last night — the singing stopped. Thank you for letting her rest.'

k: Sing to the sea sometimes. It's still listening, wherever it went.
src: 'Sing to the sea sometimes. It\'s still listening, wherever it went.'

k: A slab of crest-glass, crusted white with old salt, wedged in the rock like a figurehead. Something inside it is singing.
src: 'A slab of crest-glass, crusted white with old salt, wedged in the rock like a figurehead. Something inside it is singing.'

k: Water that is not there rises around the glass — and in it, a drowned woman in a Cantor's robe, still singing the boats home.
src: 'Water that is not there rises around the glass — and in it, a drowned woman in a Cantor\'s robe, still singing the boats home.'

k: The song ends on a long, low note, like a tide turning. The crest-glass clears, and in it burns a Crest none of you has ever seen: three waves, each over the last.
src: 'The song ends on a long, low note, like a tide turning. The crest-glass clears, and in it burns a Crest none of you has ever seen: three waves, each over the last.'

k: The crest-glass is clear and quiet now. If you listen very hard, it still sounds a little like the sea.
src: 'The crest-glass is clear and quiet now. If you listen very hard, it still sounds a little like the sea.'

k: At the end of the Strait That Was, the Drowned Cantor sang over a lost Crest. We let her finish her song. The Tidecaller calling is ours to carry now.
src: 'At the end of the Strait That Was, the Drowned Cantor sang over a lost Crest. We let her finish her song. The Tidecaller calling is ours to carry now.'

k: Hask. Last of the founders' guild. Well — last of anything, these days.
src: 'Hask. Last of the founders\' guild. Well — last of anything, these days.'

k: Every bell in this city was poured by Bellwrights. That was a calling once, child — a Crest. Then the Choir decided a bell that could call the faithful could call other things too.
src: 'Every bell in this city was poured by Bellwrights. That was a calling once, child — a Crest. Then the Choir decided a bell that could call the faithful could call other things too.'

k: They struck the calling from the rolls and walled the guild's crest-glass up in the old foundry under the Undercroft, with the Abbot to watch it. The Abbot is a bell. Don't ask.
src: 'They struck the calling from the rolls and walled the guild\'s crest-glass up in the old foundry under the Undercroft, with the Abbot to watch it. The Abbot is a bell. Don\'t ask.'

k: The flood opened the walls. If you're going down there anyway... ring it for me. Once. That's all I've ever wanted.
src: 'The flood opened the walls. If you\'re going down there anyway... ring it for me. Once. That\'s all I\'ve ever wanted.'

k: Founder Hask in the ruins of Aurenne says the Bellwrights' crest-glass is walled up in the far north-east of the drowned Undercroft, watched by the Bronze Abbot.
src: 'Founder Hask in the ruins of Aurenne says the Bellwrights\' crest-glass is walled up in the far north-east of the drowned Undercroft, watched by the Bronze Abbot.'

k: North-east corner of the drowned Undercroft, past the old reliquary. You'll hear it before you see it.
src: 'North-east corner of the drowned Undercroft, past the old reliquary. You\'ll hear it before you see it.'

k: I heard it. All the way up here, through the ash. First time in four hundred years that bell has rung for anyone but the Choir.
src: 'I heard it. All the way up here, through the ash. First time in four hundred years that bell has rung for anyone but the Choir.'

k: Go on, then, Bellwright. Make some noise.
src: 'Go on, then, Bellwright. Make some noise.'

k: A bell of crest-glass, taller than a man, hangs in a cage of rusted chain. Before it, something bronze stirs on its yoke.
src: 'A bell of crest-glass, taller than a man, hangs in a cage of rusted chain. Before it, something bronze stirs on its yoke.'

k: The Bronze Abbot swings down from the dark, ringing with every step it takes.
src: 'The Bronze Abbot swings down from the dark, ringing with every step it takes.'

k: The Abbot cracks down the middle with a sound like the last bell of evening. The chains fall away. In the glass bell burns a Crest you have never seen: a bell, mid-swing, ringing.
src: 'The Abbot cracks down the middle with a sound like the last bell of evening. The chains fall away. In the glass bell burns a Crest you have never seen: a bell, mid-swing, ringing.'

k: The glass bell hangs free now. Touch it, and it hums.
src: 'The glass bell hangs free now. Touch it, and it hums.'

k: Under Aurenne we rang the bell the founders hid. Hask heard it. The Bellwright calling is ours now.
src: 'Under Aurenne we rang the bell the founders hid. Hask heard it. The Bellwright calling is ours now.'

k: Kiteholm flies kites because kites are what we have. But there were folk who flew more than kites, once. Kitewrights.
src: 'Kiteholm flies kites because kites are what we have. But there were folk who flew more than kites, once. Kitewrights.'

k: The Choir struck them out. "Only the sun belongs in the sky." Burned the workshops. One didn't burn — it was already too far down to reach.
src: 'The Choir struck them out. "Only the sun belongs in the sky." Burned the workshops. One didn\'t burn — it was already too far down to reach.'

k: It's in the Underhang. Deep. The south end. With the thing they built to lift it, which never lifted anything but grudges.
src: 'It\'s in the Underhang. Deep. The south end. With the thing they built to lift it, which never lifted anything but grudges.'

k: If you find their crest-glass, bring the calling back up. Let somebody fly who isn't a kite.
src: 'If you find their crest-glass, bring the calling back up. Let somebody fly who isn\'t a kite.'

k: Ada Kestrel in Kiteholm says the Kitewrights' last workshop lies at the far south end of the Underhang, guarded by the Scrap Colossus.
src: 'Ada Kestrel in Kiteholm says the Kitewrights\' last workshop lies at the far south end of the Underhang, guarded by the Scrap Colossus.'

k: South, as deep as the Underhang goes. Mind the lines.
src: 'South, as deep as the Underhang goes. Mind the lines.'

k: Look at you. A Kitewright. Gaffer Quill is going to be unbearable about this — he always said they'd come back.
src: 'Look at you. A Kitewright. Gaffer Quill is going to be unbearable about this — he always said they\'d come back.'

k: Go on. Fall upward.
src: 'Go on. Fall upward.'

k: A workshop hangs in the dark, all struts and old canvas, half-swallowed by the rock. At its heart, a slab of crest-glass shaped like a wing.
src: 'A workshop hangs in the dark, all struts and old canvas, half-swallowed by the rock. At its heart, a slab of crest-glass shaped like a wing.'

k: Something huge unfolds out of the scrap around the glass, rivets screaming.
src: 'Something huge unfolds out of the scrap around the glass, rivets screaming.'

k: The Colossus sags, then sits, almost gently, as if it had only ever wanted to be allowed to stop. The wing-shaped glass clears. In it burns a Crest: a kite on a long line.
src: 'The Colossus sags, then sits, almost gently, as if it had only ever wanted to be allowed to stop. The wing-shaped glass clears. In it burns a Crest: a kite on a long line.'
